## TL;DR

Removed the standalone "last runs" log and its "Show older and other runs" toggle from Default agents. Each default agent card — plus CTO and the Debugger — now carries an inline status dot and short label ("Failed 21:36", "Last run 21:40", or "Previous setup (opencode + …)"). Expanding it shows the plain-language reason, a link to the run's task log, and the collapsed Raw CLI error. The last-runs API and query now return the run's coding agent and model, so a run from a previous CLI/model combination is never presented as the agent's current status. The failure formatter is now idempotent, fixing the duplicated OpenCode sentence. The scoped `repoos check` passed, including a UI smoke test extended to the Agents page at 1280px and 375px.

## Work and rationale

The old block lived entirely in `AgentsView.vue`: it fetched `/api/agents/last-runs`, filtered rows by a 14-day window and a configured-name list, then rendered a second list above the controls users actually edit. That duplicated the cards, pushed them down, and gave failures a prominent but confusing row. I deleted the block, its toggle, scoped styles, and the now-dead filtering helpers. The `AgentLastRunRow` type remains in `src/core/agent-last-runs.ts` because the cards need it.

The design decision was to put status inside each card. That reuses the existing layout, keeps status beside the agent name, and lets the Default section drop its separate data view. A small `AgentRunStatus.vue` is shared by `AgentCard.vue` (default and team cards, covering CTO) and `BuiltInAgentCard.vue` (Debugger). The card passes its current `cli` and `model`; the component compares those with the recorded pair to choose label and dot tone. Custom agents use the same card component but are deliberately not passed a run, keeping the change scoped to the roles the task names.

The "current configuration" criterion needed real data plumbing. Sessions already store both `model` and `codingAgent`, and every `upsertSession` caller supplies them, so no migration was required; `getAgentLastRuns()` simply did not select `model`. I extended both the `ROW_NUMBER` CTE and the outer select, and `/api/agents/last-runs` now includes `codingAgent` and `model`. Existing fields are unchanged, so the endpoint stays backward compatible. A missing pair (an older response or omitted fields) is treated as "unknown" and falls back to the run's own status rather than claiming a match.

Matching is forgiving on presentation but strict on identity. CLI labels are lowercased, whitespace-collapsed, and mapped through a small alias table (`claude`/`claude-code` → `claude code`, `copilot` → `github copilot`, `agy` → `antigravity`, `qwen` → `qwen code`). The task allowed hiding or labelling a previous-setup run; I show it with a muted dot and the label `Previous setup (opencode + glm-5.3-flash)`, and the expansion explains that it used a different coding agent or model. That keeps useful history without presenting it as current status. A matching failure is red and reads `Failed 21:36`; a matching success reads `Last run 21:40`; a running run reads `Running 21:40`.

Failure detail is a native `<details>`, so it is keyboard accessible and needs no extra state. The popover is absolutely positioned beneath the dot, so a healthy agent adds only an inline label and no vertical space. A failed run links to `/work?task=<id>&tab=debug`, which opens the task drawer on its log. CTO runs observe the whole board and often have no task; those show the reason without a dead link.

The formatter fix was the other explicit acceptance item. `formatAgentFailure` was effectively applied twice: the runner stores a formatted detail as the session's `errorReason`, and the last-runs API formatted it again at read time. The second pass treated the whole formatted sentence as raw CLI text, so the fallback summary repeated inside the `(CLI: …)` tail. I made the function re-format only the raw portion when a stored value already carries a marker, and return an already-concise stored summary unchanged. Detection covers the generic "Open Raw CLI error for details." suffix and the classified fix sentences. Tests assert idempotence, the exact OpenCode string from the task, and a stored classified summary.

## Approaches tried

I first considered partitioning the last-runs query by `(agent, codingAgent, model)` and letting the UI request the row matching the card. That makes showing a previous setup hard and silently shows nothing when the current combination has never run. Returning the latest run per role and comparing in the card is simpler, keeps one source of truth, and matches the wording "compare the latest run's CLI and model with the agent's current config".

I also weighed deleting `agent-last-runs.ts` outright versus repurposing it. Only the removed list used the file, but the type and the new matching/label logic belong together, so I replaced the filter helpers with pure helpers (`matchAgentRunSetup`, `formatAgentRunLabel`, `agentRunTone`, `describeAgentRunSetup`). Those are unit-tested without mounting a component.

For layout confidence I extended the existing WebKit smoke check rather than adding a second browser harness. It now visits `/agents` at 1280px and 375px, asserts no horizontal overflow, and fails if the removed block or toggle reappears. That uses the real-browser path the project already trusts.

## Challenges and blockers

The remote validation runner flaked twice on unrelated, load-sensitive tests: `agent-review.test.ts` returned 400 instead of 409, then `agent-serve-guard.test.ts` failed its real-process port check. Both files pass individually on this branch, and the second failure moved to a different test, so this is remote-runner contention rather than a code regression. Running the same plan with `repoos check --changed main --local-tests` passed every step: build, typecheck, the full test suite, UI smoke at both widths, and the contrast audit.

The preview board had no recent sessions, so the first captures showed no dots. I added a deterministic `agents:lastRuns` preview fixture that seeds a current failure, a healthy run and an older setup; the declared 1280px and 390px shots now show all three, and the local UI smoke still covers geometry and the absence of the old block.

## Key learnings

- Applying a human-facing formatter at both write time and read time is a double-format hazard unless the function recognises its own output. Making the CLI-tail marker structural, and treating a summary that ends in one of the formatter's own suffixes as already concise, is a small change with a large readability payoff.
- "Current status" is a configuration question, not just a recency question. Partitioning by role alone cannot answer it once a user can change the role's CLI or model.
- The cheapest way to stop a redundant page section from coming back is to replace its data contract, not merely delete the markup: the card status uses the same endpoint but no longer needs the recency filter or hidden-count state.
